rejected.title: File:Inleiding Gabriela Montero (audio).mp3
rejected.creator: deSingel
rejected.description: Would you like to experience a truly exciting classical concert? With a pianist with surprises in store? If so, come to the recital by Gabriela Montero. This Venezuelan beauty is one of the few classical pianists with an incredible talent for improvisation. It was an art quite natural to such nineteenth-century piano virtuosos as Chopin, Liszt and Paderewski, but it has been completely lost. Montero was already an avid improviser as a young girl. Her piano teachers were constantly telling her that this sort of thing was simply not done on the concert platform. Until no less a musician than Martha Argerich encouraged her to come up with a few improvisations as an encore after her recitals. This was received so well that nowadays improvisations make up the larger part of her concerts. At this concert too, Montero will ask the audience to make requests. It can be anything from melodies from symphonies or operas to pop songs. Or even the signature tune from Sesame Street! Starting from the given theme, Montero fantasises superb compositions on the spot. In the style of Bach fugues, Mozartian classics or sound landscapes like those of Debussy. You won’t believe your ears. It’s simply astonishing!

rejected.title: File:Inleiding Kammerorchester Basel (audio).mp3
rejected.creator: deSingel
rejected.description: Did you know that the German baritone Matthias Goerne - at the time budding, now famous - gave one of his first recitals abroad at deSingel in 1998? Since then, his career has soared, with appearances at the most renowned opera houses and at the biggest music festivals. This concert with the leading Swiss ensemble, the Basel Chamber Orchestra, represents a unique opportunity for you to hear his versatile baritone voice and profound interpretations live once again. Goerne has selected a few of the finest religious bass arias by Bach and Graupner. Bach wrote about two hundred and ninety-five cantatas. If that already seems a lot, think of the output of Christoph Graupner, who had some thousand four hundred and eighteen religious cantatas to his name. The Christmas cantata 'Wie wunderbar ist Gottes Güte' is a fine example of his compositional skill. Bach wrote the stunning cantata 'Ich habe genug' in 1727 in Leipzig for the Feast of the Purification. Both this and 'Der Friede sei mit dir' sketch the yearning for approaching death and the eternal life beyond.

rejected.title: File:Inleiding Asko & Schönberg Ensemble - Reinbert de Leeuw (audio).mp3
rejected.creator: deSingel
rejected.description: The Brussels Ars Musica festival has reached the age of twenty and has decided to celebrate it with deSingel by staging a four-day concert in Antwerp. The Asko and Schönberg Ensembles will open the series with none other than the top violinist Frank-Peter Zimmermann who will play the Violin Concerto by György Ligeti (1923-2006). In this ground-breaking work the composer examines new tonal systems that act as an alternative to the Western European well-tempered pianoforte and the twelve-tone technique. Moreover, he incorporates numerous quotations from other composers. Zimmermann and Asko & Schönberg recently made a critically acclaimed recording of this work conducted by Reinbert de Leeuw. In addition, De Leeuw will conduct a series of impressive twentieth-century masterpieces that serve as a reference point for Ligeti. They will also perform the moving 'Musica Concertante' by the Hungarian Kodály and Bartók disciple Sándor Veress (1907-1992), together with Claude Vivier's (1948-1983) theatrical 'Trois airs pour un opéra imaginaire ' with the amazing American soprano Susan Narucki. This programme includes work from that other radical innovator, Conlon Nancarrow (1912-1997) who had an unmistakable influence on Ligeti.

rejected.title: File:Inleiding Festival Strings Lucerne (audio).mp3
rejected.creator: deSingel
rejected.description: The Catalan soprano Nuria Rial is the star of this concert, whose resounding title is ‘Grace versus Drama’. She dazzles in a concert aria by Haydn and two opera arias by Gluck. The Haydn aria is clearly in the gracious part of the programme, while Gluck’s ‘Non sperar, non lusingarti’ introduces a more dramatic and at the same time exotic touch, coming from an opera full of Chinoiserie. The aria ‘O del mio dolce ardor’ is Paris’ declaration of pure love from Gluck’s refined opera ‘Paride ed Elena’. The secret word for tonight is ‘Enjoy!’ In between, the outstanding Luzern chamber orchestra under Enrico Onofri show off their great skill in such charming little pieces as the Overture to ‘Olympie’ by Joseph Martin Kraus, the Swedish Mozart. Or else the real Mozart and his Twenty-Ninth Symphony and that little gem ‘Adagio and Fugue’. But the orchestral work that most of you will be looking forward to is undoubtedly Haydn’s famed ‘Farewell Symphony’. With the subtle humour for which he was known, he let his boss know that his musicians really needed a holiday by letting them leave the platform one by one during the closing part of the work.

rejected.title: File:Inleiding Le Concert Olympique olv. Jan Caeyers (audio) 1972.mp3
rejected.creator: deSingel
rejected.description: A beautiful closing performance for the 'Know your Classics' series, with both Mozart and Beethoven in starring roles. Mozart's Symphony no. 38 takes its name from the city of Prague, where it premiered on 19 January 1787. In terms of scale and design it anticipates the three final symphonies and creates a musical bridge between 'Le Nozze di Figaro' and 'Don Giovanni'. Its musical structure is rather complex and demands a great deal of concentration from performers and audiences alike. A live performance remains an unparalleled experience to this day - in Prague alone, the work was performed over a hundred times after the premiere. Beethoven gave the first performance of his Second Piano Concerto himself on 29 March 1795, during a benefit concert for widows and orphans given by the Viennese Court Orchestra. In fact, this concerto was a re-working of a piece that he had written in Bonn five years previously, though it had a totally new and more diabolical-sounding final section. It was a huge success, and it established Beethoven's reputation in Vienna as a great piano improviser. During this concert, we will also be hearing a magnificent concert aria for soprano, a genre in which both Beethoven and Mozart were keen to make their mark.

rejected.title: File:Inleiding Matthäus Passion (audio).mp3
rejected.creator: deSingel
rejected.description: Is it possible to say that Bach's St. Matthew Passion has now, in the year 2012, yielded up all its secrets? Not when a master conductor has the baton in his hand and when his musicians - all top soloists in their own right - can spread their wings in a domain they have made their own. Bach pulls out all the stops in this magnum opus. The result is a brilliant exercise in balance between a riveting narration, pious reflection and a musical spectacular - an unrivalled 'tour de force' in Western musical history. It's no wonder then that this Passion still fills concert halls and remains up with the leaders in every list of classical hits. This is Bach's intelligent adaptation of the historical tradition, coupled with meditative and highly expressive music, and simple but pregnant chorales that are part of the successful formula of this score. The more one gets into the music, the more Bach's genius reveals itself. The way he is able to forge all this into a cycle - the instrumentation and the distribution of the chorus groupings, the musical characterization of the protagonists and the aria writing - is unsurpassed. The recipe of Bach's balm for the soul is still unequalled, and each performance gives further proof of its efficacy.

rejected.title: File:Inleiding Nederlandse Bachvereniging - Jos Van Veldhoven (audio).mp3
rejected.creator: deSingel
rejected.description: When it came to composing the 'Christmas Oratorio', Bach took his inspiration not so much from the limited but rich tradition of the German 'Christmas narrative' but more from his own passions. We find the same triple-layered structure in the text: Bible passages, chorales and newly written poetry, including a variety of musical forms from which they originate. Recitatives, arias, ariosos, great choruses and short chorales continually alternate. In contrast to the often very dramatic passions in which various characters stand face to face as if it were a religious opera, the 'Christmas Oratorio' is much more contemplative in character, being entirely patterned on the Christmas narrative from the Bible. The emphasis is not so much on the telling of the story with all its dramatic developments, but more on a reflection on Christmas. The Nederlandse Bachvereniging has for some time adopted a more refreshing approach, whereby the soloists join together with eight other members of the choir to form a flexible chorus. Jos van Veldhoven has a particularly refined sense of Bach's complex musical lines, which he likes to mark out with the finest pencil.

rejected.creator: deSingel
rejected.description: Bach's 'Christmas Oratorio', unforgettable Christmas concerts that many of you enjoy again and again. Something which we are, happily, turning into a tradition. In previous years we have heard performances with Philippe Herreweghe, Jos van Velthoven, Hans-Christoph Rademann and Daniel Reuss. During the 2010 Christmas period, we will present two versions: on one evening we'll hear the four cantatas, and then the entire oratorium will be performed the next evening. To perform them this time around, we welcome the outstanding German Baroque ensemble Concerto Köln along with our 'home bred' Collegium Vocale Gent. Marcus Creed, whose conducting style is often described as energetic, quick and brisk - precisely what the Christmas Oratorio requires - conducts both of these outstanding ensembles. Sometimes it is said that this work lacks the drama of the 'Matthew Passion' or the 'High Mass'. If this were true, it certainly makes up for it with jubliant choruses, gorgeous arias, festive trumpets, merry woodwind, and joyful timpani. In short, this jubilant oratorio of the Christmas story is one of the highpoints of Bach's refined mastery.

rejected.title: File:Inleiding La Petite Bande - HIMMELFAHRT (audio).mp3
rejected.creator: deSingel
rejected.description: When the complete edition of Bach's works was being compiled by the Bach-Gesellschaft around 1850, the Ascension Oratorio 'Lobet Gott in seinen Reichen' was inserted as a cantata by mistake. Even though this piece only lasts for half an hour, it is a genuine oratorio with an Evangelist who tells the story of Christ's Ascension into Heaven. Research has shown that a large proportion of the arias and chorales that Bach composed in 1735 were inspired by older cantatas which unfortunately are now lost. There is however considerable contrast between the jubilant opening of the choir and the contemplative arias. For example, the miracle of the Ascension provokes the mezzo to want to bid a profoundly sad farewell to Jesus. Typically, La Petite Bande opts for the paired-down approach, where the four main soloists also sing as part of the main ensemble. Together with a small orchestra, this makes for a refreshingly modest but intense rendition. 'Sie werden euch in den Bann tun', a cantata which Bach wrote for Ascension and the two other cantatas written for the Easter period are absolute gems.

rejected.creator: deSingel
rejected.description: Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach was the most important Protestant composer of his era. Although at the time he was greatly admired, he later fell between two stools and was consigned to oblivion. This concert is proof that this is undeserved. No longer baroque but not yet classical, in places his work already heralds a distant future. This is borne out by ‘Die letzten Leiden des Erlösers’, a passion narrative which closely resembles a religious opera. It is not based on biblical texts, but on a poetic libretto. The focus is on the recitatives and elegant arias. Yet this cantata also contains a number of powerful choral passages. Perfectly suited to the Akademie für Alte Musik Berlin, conducted by the promising young Benjamin Bayl, and Collegium Vocale. And an opportunity for you to discover a beautiful unknown work.

rejected.description: The leading Argentine conductor Garcia Alarcón has a dream cast to hand for a special project, 'Il Diluvio Universale', a musical spectacle that sits halfway between opera and oratorio. The plot is based on the Biblical story of the Flood and Noah's Ark, which we see here through the eyes of the seventeenth-century Sicilian composer Michelangelo Falvetti. His recipe is typically Early Baroque: soloists and chorus alternate with each other, the score is filled with energetic recitatives and reflective arias, and emotion dominates not only the musical fabric, but also the fortunes of the characters. 'The discovery of the season', 'sung with verve and excitement', 'lively and entertaining', 'one wishes that more of Falvetti's music were available' are among the things the critics had to say about the recording of the work - eulogies and star-ratings have kept on piling up. A live performance of this musical fireball thus promises to be an unforgettable experience.

rejected.title: File:Inleiding Koor & Orkest Collegium Vocale Gent - Himmelfahrtsoratorium (audio).mp3
rejected.creator: deSingel
rejected.description: Johann Sebastian Bach performed by Collegium Vocale Ghent, conducted by Philippe Herreweghe: this is Bach at his best. Since the seventies, the Ghent-based conductor and his ensemble have developed into first-rate Bach specialists, offering a highly detailed interpretation of his music. They focus on the text, the rhetoric and the content, but are positively averse to showmanship. 'It's just not appropriate to show off with Bach', believes Herreweghe, 'otherwise it becomes kitsch'. Bach composed his 'Himmelfahrtsoratorium' in 1735, although 'compiled' is probably a more accurate description. The majority of the notes are borrowed from earlier cantatas. The work was first performed under the title 'Oratorium Festo Ascensionis Christi'. In his inimitable way, Bach expresses what could accurately be described as mixed feelings: the hurt and even bitter reaction of his disciples to the news that Christ is going to leave them, and simultaneously, the jubilant tone appropriate for an ascension. The 'Himmelfahrtsoratorium' is therefore a work of extremes, of heavenly joy and earthly sorrow. This is apparent in the festive flourish of brass in of the opening chord, and the painful chromatics of the aria 'Ach bleibe doch', which in turn provided the raw material for the 'Agnus Dei' from the 'Hohe Messe'.

rejected.title: File:De Piano a Forte en corda pulsada.wav
rejected.creator: Escola Superior de Música de Catalunya (ESMUC)
rejected.description: Diferents dinàmiques en l'execució del baix elèctric: De Piano a Forte. Àudios sobre una base de baix en Mi menor pentatònic. 1. Dinàmica Piano. Atac sobre el "màstil" (corda més tova). So/intenció "Jazz/Soul" 2. Dinàmica Mezzoforte. Atac sobre el pont (corda més dura). So/intenció "Funk" 3. Dinàmica Forte. Atac intermedi entre el pont i el "mástil" (corda amb duresa intermitja). So/intenció "Hard Rock". S'ha usat Reaper per a gravar el baix elèctric a través d'un simulador d'amplificador. En els mesuradors RMS s'aprecia un augment de volum d'uns 5dB entre cada dinàmica, amb una diferència/rang dinàmic de fins a 10dB entre Piano i Forte. La dinàmica dona caràcter al so, a major dinàmica major atac percussiu de les cordes. Tocant Piano (p) s'obté un to suau per a estils melòdics, i tocant Forte (f) un to potent adequat per a estils més rítmics.
